source_text: Παντὶ τοίνυν σθένει ὁ τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος παιδαγωγός, ὁ θεῖος ἡμῶν λόγος, πάσῃ καταχρώμενος σοφίας μηχανῇ, σῴζειν ἐπιβέβληται τοὺς νηπίους, νουθετῶν, ἐπιτιμῶν, ἐπιπλήττων, ἐλέγχων, ἀπειλούμενος, ἰώμενος, ἐπαγγελλόμενος, χαριζόμενος, »πολλοῖς τισιν οἱονεὶ χαλινοῖς« τὰς ἀλόγους τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος »δεσμεύων« ὁρμάς. συνελόντι γοῦν εἰπεῖν, οὕτως ὁ κύριος πρὸς ἡμᾶς, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς πρὸς τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν. »τέκνα σοί ἐστιν; παίδευσον αὐτά«, ἡ σοφία παραινεῖ, »καὶ κάμψον αὐτὰ ἐκ νεότητος αὐτῶν. θυγατέρες σοί εἰσι; πρόσεχε τῷ σώματι αὐτῶν, καὶ μὴ ἱλαρώσῃς πρὸς αὐτὰς τὸ πρόσωπόν σου.« καίτοι τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν, υἱούς τε καὶ θυγατέρας, σφόδρα καὶ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὁτιοῦν ἀγαπῶμεν. ἐπεὶ δ᾿ οἱ μὲν πρὸς χάριν ὁμιλοῦντες ὀλίγον ἀγαπῶσιν ὃ μὴ λυποῦσιν, οἱ δὲ πρὸς ὠφέλειαν ἐπιστύφοντες, εἰ καὶ παραυτίκα λυπηροί, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸν ἔπειτα εὐεργετοῦσιν αἰῶνα, οὐ τὴν παραυτίκα ἡδονὴν ὁ κύριος, ἀλλὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐσκόπησε τρυφήν. ἐπίωμεν δὲ ἤδη καὶ τὸν τρόπον αὐτοῦ τῆς φιλανθρώπου παιδαγωγίας μετὰ μαρτυρίας προφητικῆς. Νουθέτησις μὲν οὖν ἐστιν ψόγος κηδεμονικός, νοῦ ἐμποιητικός. τοιοῦτος ὁ παιδαγωγὸς νουθετῶν, ὡς κἀν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ λέγων »ποσάκις ἠθέλησα συναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις συνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε«. αὖθίς τε ἡ γραφὴ νουθετεῖ, »καὶ ἐμοίχευον« λέγουσα »τὸ ξύλον καὶ τὸν λίθον, καὶ ἐθυμίασαν τῇ Βάαλ«. μέγιστον γὰρ τεκμήριον τῆς φιλανθρωπίας αὐτοῦ, ὅτι καίτοι σαφῶς εἰδὼς τὴν ἀναισχυντίαν τοῦ ἐκλακτίσαντος λαοῦ καὶ ἀποσκιρτήσαντος, ὅμως ἐπὶ τὴν μετάνοιαν παρακαλεῖ καί φησιν διὰ τοῦ Ἰεζεκιήλ· »υἱὲ ἀνθρώπου, ἐν μέσῳ σκορπίων σὺ κατοικεῖς, πλὴν λάλησον αὐτοῖς, ἐὰν ἄρα ἀκούσωσιν.« ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ Μωυσεῖ »πορεύου« φησὶν »καὶ εἰπὲ τῷ Φαραώ, ἵνα ἐξαποστείλῃ τὸν λαόν, ἐγὼ δὲ οἶδα ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἐξαποστείλῃ αὐτούς«. ἐμφαίνει γὰρ ἄμφω, καὶ τὸ θεῖον προειδὼς τὸ ἐσόμενον, καὶ τὸ φιλάνθρωπον τὸ αὑτοῦ τῷ αὐτεξουσίῳ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀφορμὰς μετανοίας χαριζόμενος. νουθετεῖ δὲ καὶ διὰ Ἡσαΐου κηδόμενος τοῦ λαοῦ, ὁπηνίκα λέγει· »ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσιν αὐτῶν τιμῶσί με, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἐστὶν ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ« (τοῦτό ἐστι ψόγος ἐλεγκτικός)· »μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.« ἐνταῦθα ἡ κηδεμονία φανερώσασα τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ παραλλήλου δείκνυσι τὴν σωτηρίαν. Ἐπιτίμησις δέ ἐστι ψόγος ἐπ᾿ αἰσχροῖς οἰκειῶν πρὸς τὰ καλά. τοῦτο ἐνδείκνυται διὰ Ἱερεμίου· »ἵπποι θηλυμανεῖς ἐγενήθησαν, ἕκαστος ἐπὶ τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ ἐχρεμέτιζεν. μὴ ἐπὶ τούτοις οὐκ ἐπισκέψομαι; λέγει κύριος· ἢ ἐν λαῷ τῷ τοιούτῳ οὐκ ἐκδικήσει ἡ ψυχή μου;« παραπλέκει δὲ πανταχοῦ τὸν φόβον, ὅτι »φόβος κυρίου ἀρχὴ αἰσθήσεως«. καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ὠσηὲ »οὐκ ἐπισκέψομαι« φησίν »αὐτούς· ὅτι αὐτοὶ μετὰ τῶν πορνῶν συνεφύροντο καὶ μετὰ τῶν τετελεσμένων ἔθυον, καὶ ὁ λαὸς ὁ συνίων συνεπλέκετο πόρνῃ«. δείκνυσιν αὐτῶν φανερώτερον τὸ ἁμάρτημα, συνιέναι αὐτοὺς ὁμολογῶν, ὡς ἑκόντας ἁμαρτάνοντας. καὶ ἡ σύνεσις ὄψις ἐστὶ ψυχῆς. διὸ καὶ ὁ Ἰσραὴλ ὁ ὁρῶν τὸν θεόν, τουτέστιν ὁ συνίων τὸν θεόν. Μέμψις δέ ἐστι ψόγος ὡς ὀλιγωρούντων ἢ ἀμελούντων. κέχρηται τῷ τρόπῳ τούτῳ τῆς παιδαγωγίας διὰ Ἡσαΐου λέγων· »ἄκουε, οὐρανέ, καὶ ἐνωτίζου, γῆ, ὅτι κύριος ἐλάλησεν· υἱοὺς ἐγέννησα καὶ ὕψωσα, αὐτοὶ δέ με ἠθέτησαν. ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον καὶ ὄνος τὴν φάτνην τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω.« πῶς γὰρ οὐ δεινόν, εἰ ὁ εἰδὼς τὸν θεὸν οὐ γνώσεται τὸν κύριον, ἀλλ᾿ ὁ μὲν βοῦς καὶ ὁ ὄνος, τὰ νωθῆ ζῷα καὶ τὰ μωρά, εἴσεται τὸν τρέφοντα, ὁ δὲ Ἰσραὴλ ἀλογώτερος καὶ τούτων εὑρεθήσεται; καὶ διὰ Ἱερεμίου πολλὰ καταμεμψάμενος τὸν λαὸν ἐπιφέρει· »καὶ ἐμὲ ἐγκατέλιπον, λέγει κύριος.« Ἐπίπληξις δέ ἐστιν ἐπιτίμησις ἐπιπληκτικὴ ἢ ψόγος πληκτικός, κέχρηται δὲ καὶ ταύτῃ τῇ θεραπείᾳ ὁ παιδαγωγὸς διὰ Ἡσαΐου λέγων· »οὐαὶ τέκνα ἀποστάται, τάδε λέγει κύριος· ἐποιήσατε βουλὴν οὐ δι᾿ ἐμοῦ, καὶ συνθήκας οὐ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματός μου.« στύμματι δὲ αὐστηροτάτῳ παρ᾿ ἕκαστα προσχρῆται τῷ φόβῳ, ἀναστομῶν ἅμα καὶ ἐπιστρέφων δι᾿ αὐτοῦ πρὸς σωτηρίαν τὸν λαόν, καθάπερ καὶ τὰ βαπτόμενα τῶν ἐρίων προστύφεσθαι φιλεῖ εἰς βεβαίαν εὐτρεπιζόμενα τῆς βαφῆς παραδοχήν.
thought_title: Beneficence and Punishment of the Same Power
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, the divine Logos, our Pedagogue of humanity, using every device of wisdom, has been entrusted to save the infants, admonishing, rebuking, striking, convicting, threatening, healing, promising, and giving graciously, as if binding the irrational impulses of humanity with many reins. To put it briefly, the Lord is to us as we are to our children. Wisdom advises, 'Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend them from their youth. Do you have daughters? Watch over their bodies, and do not show them a cheerful face.' Although we love our children, sons and daughters, very much and more than anything, those who associate with them for pleasure love them little, because they do not grieve them, while those who care for them for their benefit, even if they cause them grief for the moment, benefit them for the future age. The Lord did not consider the present pleasure, but the future one. Let us also examine the manner of the philanthropic pedagogy of the Logos, with prophetic testimony. Admonition is a paternal rebuke, imparting mind. Such is the Pedagogue, admonishing, as also in the Gospel, saying, 'How often I wanted to gather your children, as a bird gathers its nestlings under its wings, and you were not willing.' Again, the Scripture admonishes, saying, 'They committed adultery with the tree and the stone, and they burned incense to Baal.' This is the greatest proof of His philanthropy, that although He clearly knew the shamelessness of the people who were chosen and had revolted, He still calls them to repentance and says through Ezekiel, 'Son of man, you dwell among scorpions; nevertheless, speak to them, whether they will hear or not.' And also to Moses, 'Go and say to Pharaoh, that he may let the people go; but I know that he will not let them go.' He shows both, the divine foreknowledge of what is to come, and the philanthropic giving of opportunities for repentance to the soul. He also admonishes through Isaiah, caring for the people, when He says, 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me' (this is a rebuking rebuke); 'but in vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.' Here, the care, having revealed the sin, shows the salvation. Rebuke is a rebuke on account of shameful things, familiarly urging towards the good. This is shown through Jeremiah: 'The horses have become lustful stallions, each one neighing after his neighbor's wife. Shall I not punish them for these things?' says the Lord; 'and shall I not avenge myself on such a nation?' He also brings fear everywhere, because 'the fear of the Lord is the beginning of perception.' And again through Hosea, 'I will not punish them, for they have mixed with prostitutes and sacrificed with the polluted; and the people who understand have been entangled with a prostitute.' He shows their sin more clearly, confessing that they understand, as if they sin willingly. And understanding is the vision of the soul. Therefore, Israel, who sees God, that is, who understands God. Blame is a rebuke as if they were neglecting or disregarding. The Logos uses this manner of pedagogy through Isaiah, saying, 'Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I have begotten and brought up sons, but they have rebelled against me. The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know me.' For how is it not terrible, if one who knows God does not recognize the Lord, but the ox and the donkey, dull and foolish animals, know their feeder, and Israel is found to be more irrational than these? And through Jeremiah, having blamed the people much, He says, 'And they have forsaken me, says the Lord.' Striking is a rebuking rebuke, or a striking rebuke. The Pedagogue also uses this treatment through Isaiah, saying, 'Woe to the rebellious children, thus says the Lord: you have made a plan not through me, and a covenant not through my Spirit.' With the most severe threat, He uses fear for each thing, at the same time turning and returning the people to salvation through it, just as the wool that is being dyed is wont to be roughened, so that it may be receptive to the dye and become durable.

pass_b_english: The divine Word, our Pedagogue of humanity, employs every device of wisdom with all His strength, entrusted with the task of saving the immature. He admonishes, rebukes, strikes, convicts, threatens, heals, promises, and bestows grace, binding the irrational impulses of humanity as if with many reins. To put it briefly, the Lord relates to us just as we relate to our own children. Wisdom advises: "Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend them from their youth. Do you have daughters? Watch over their bodies, and do not show them a cheerful face." Although we love our children—sons and daughters—exceedingly and above all else, those who keep company with them for pleasure love them little because they do not grieve them, whereas those who correct them for their benefit, even if they cause momentary grief, do them good for the age to come. The Lord did not look to the present pleasure, but to the future one.

Let us now also examine the manner of His philanthropic pedagogy with prophetic testimony. Admonition is a fatherly rebuke that implants understanding. Such is the Pedagogue when He admonishes, as also in the Gospel He says: "How often I wanted to gather your children, as a bird gathers its nestlings under its wings, and you were not willing." Again, Scripture admonishes, saying: "They committed adultery with the tree and the stone, and they burned incense to Baal." This is the greatest proof of His philanthropy: although He clearly knew the shamelessness of the people who kicked against Him and revolted, He still calls them to repentance and says through Ezekiel: "Son of man, you dwell among scorpions; nevertheless, speak to them, whether perhaps they will hear" (Ezekiel 2:6). And also to Moses He says: "Go and say to Pharaoh, that he may let the people go; but I know that he will not let them go." He shows both the divine foreknowledge of what is to come, and the philanthropic giving of opportunities for repentance to the self-determining soul. He also admonishes through Isaiah, caring for the people, when He says: "This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me" (this is a convicting rebuke); "but in vain do they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men." Here the care, having revealed the sin, shows the salvation.

Rebuke is a rebuke on account of shameful things, urging familiarly toward the good. This is shown through Jeremiah: "The horses have become lustful stallions, each one neighing after his neighbor's wife. Shall I not punish them for these things? says the Lord; and shall I not avenge Myself on such a nation?" (Jeremiah 5:8-9). He weaves fear in everywhere, because "the fear of the Lord is the beginning of perception." And again through Hosea: "I will not punish them, for they have mixed with prostitutes and sacrificed with the polluted; and the people who understand have been entangled with a prostitute." He shows their sin more clearly, acknowledging that they understand, as if they sin willingly. And understanding is the vision of the soul. Therefore, Israel who sees God—that is, who understands God.

Blame is a rebuke as if they were neglecting or disregarding. The Word uses this manner of pedagogy through Isaiah, saying: "Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I have begotten and brought up sons, but they have rebelled against Me. The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know Me." For how is it not terrible, if one who knows God does not recognize the Lord, but the ox and the donkey, dull and foolish animals, know their feeder, and Israel is found to be more irrational than these? And through Jeremiah, having blamed the people much, He says: "And they have forsaken Me, says the Lord." Striking is a rebuking rebuke, or a striking rebuke. The Pedagogue also uses this treatment through Isaiah, saying: "Woe to the rebellious children, thus says the Lord: you have made a plan not through Me, and a covenant not through My Spirit." With the most severe threat He employs fear for each thing, at the same time turning and returning the people to salvation through it, just as wool that is being dyed is wont to be roughened so that it may be receptive to the dye and become durable.
